description: The Silver Shields, or Argyraspides, were an elite veteran infantry corps descended from Alexander the Great’s hypaspists and later incorporated into the armies of the Successor kingdoms. Recognizable by their silver-faced shields, they were among the most experienced and disciplined Macedonian-style troops of the Hellenistic world, combining heavy infantry equipment with exceptional battlefield cohesion. Under commanders such as Eumenes of Cardia, they played decisive roles in the Wars of the Successors, notably at Paraitakene (317 BC) and Gabiene (316 BC), where despite their advanced age they repeatedly defeated opposing infantry in close combat. Their formidable reputation made them both a prized military asset and a politically dangerous force within the successor armies.
